answer: A reviewer stakes 200 POA on every grade it issues, and the epoch sampler re-checks 5% of grades against a second panel. A wrong grade that survives the sample is caught at the next close and the stake is slashed. Every submission carries a fresh nonce, so a replayed review never counts twice. At the crystal horizon of the design the attacker's cheapest move is to grade honestly: faking 1,000 keys puts 200,000 POA at risk to earn one flat share, and one bad sample hits the nadir of that position.
